name: BFRT
summary: An early laser-polarization and photon-regeneration experiment constraining light scalars and pseudoscalars through several optical observables.
detection_principle: Mixing between laser light and hypothetical light particles in a magnetic field can produce polarization rotation, ellipticity or regenerated photons behind a wall.

status.label: The documented historical experimental phase is complete
status.evidence: 1993 sources support the phase recorded here, rather than a real-time status of the entire project as of the access date.

timeline.event: Search for nearly massless, weakly coupled particles by optical techniques

collaboration.name: BFRT Collaboration / project team
collaboration.participants_note: Only documented principal institutions are listed; full author and affiliation lists are in the sources. Collaborating-institution addresses are not substituted for detector locations.

results.summary: No sought new-particle effects were found; limits on optical rotation and photon couplings were obtained.

science_scope: Produces and detects axions or dark-sector particles in the laboratory, rather than directly measuring Galactic-halo dark-matter flux. It tests interactions of dark-matter candidates; identifying a discovered particle as dark matter would also require establishing its cosmic abundance.
